<!-- pr-reviewer: 090d7df3416c714c7f95bb366e61a111fe9c6cc7 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- The root cause is correct. A row that goes through a loop vertex crosses no edge interior. The old law (`section.rs` `wall_gouge`, branch with no model) read such a row as a move inside the region.
- The fix is small and local to the no-model branch: `crosses_rim` (`section.rs:184-200`) and `Trace::through` (`arc_wall.rs:124-147`). No tolerance changed. With a part present, the keep law and the solid law judge as before.
- `through` needs all of these: the vertex is on the trace interior (within `CROSSING_TOUCH`), the vertex is not an end of the trace, and the two neighbours are strictly on opposite sides. A touch stays a gouge.
- The wrap-around index `(k + n - 1) % n` is correct. A loop has at least 3 vertices, and `Loop::new` removes consecutive repeated vertices (also the closing repeat), so a doubled vertex gives no zero-length edge.
- No unwrap, expect or panic in the new code. The files are 318 and 283 lines. The provenance line, the Changelog line, `Fixes #1659` and the decision file are present. No process file is changed, so no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is owed.

**Probes I ran (temporary tests, not committed, removed)**
- A row through a reflex vertex of an L-shaped outline: clean. This is correct, because the row crosses the rim.
- A move that ends at the reflex vertex and stops inside: `Gouge`. A move that runs along an edge and ends at the vertex: `Gouge` (the end exclusion works).
- A vertex at index 0 and a vertex at the last index, with a row through each: clean, no wrap-around error.
- A row through the tip of an inward notch (both neighbours on one side): `Gouge`.
- A row exactly along a skewed side that has a mid-side vertex (399 cases with float noise): `Gouge` in all 399.
- A single move cannot enter the wall at a vertex and turn back. A turn needs two moves, and the law reads each move by itself.

**Results merged with main** (locally; main sha 2b6e03f, the branch was already up to date; no runner was available, the runner API returned 403)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. sim lib, `boundary_arc_planes`, `boundary_arc_walls`, `boundary_walls`, `model_excess`; app `coarse_rims`, `face_stock_edge`, `real_tip_contour`, `slot_caps`, `thread_mill_rim`, `verify_arc_reading`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.
- I did the mutations again:
  - M1 (`through` always false): `boundary_walls::a_row_through_two_side_vertices...` and `face_stock_edge::a_face_row_tangent...` fail.
  - M2 (opposite-sides test removed): `boundary_walls::a_move_inside_or_only_touching_a_vertex_still_answers_to_the_walls` fails.
- M4 is not in the table because the author shows that it does not break the two part pins: the keep law in the operation layer convicts them. This is correct. The M5 mutation covers those two pins.

**Requested before merge**
- None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. The "opposite sides" test is the exact sign `su * sw < 0.0`, with no zero band. A neighbour on the trace line gives zero and is not a crossing. But a wall that runs along the trace and has a very small wobble now counts as a crossing. I used 1e-6 mm: the middle vertex on the trace, and its neighbours on opposite sides. A move centred on that wall is then excused. With a wobble of 1e-10 mm or less, the loop was simplified and the move was still a `Gouge`. The old law has the same property for an edge that crosses the trace at a very small angle (`proper_cross`), so this is not a new class of risk. Please consider a follow-up: require the neighbours to stand off the trace line by a small distance (not only a sign). I would rate it `P7`.
2. The arc branch of `Trace::through` (`arc_wall.rs:205-216`) has no direct pin. The PR body says so. A no-model Boundary arc that goes through a vertex is the only way to reach it.
3. The question of why the stock outline has vertices on its sides stays open, as the PR body says. The fix is right for any such loop.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 090d7df3416c714c7f95bb366e61a111fe9c6cc7 -->

Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge. No blockers.

This is an independent review of this head. The earlier marker at this head came from the author's own session, so it did not count.

## What looks good

- The root cause matches the repro. The last row runs exactly through two side vertices of the stock outline. It crosses no edge interior, so the old Boundary branch read it as a move inside the region. The fix adds the vertex pass to the rim crossing (`crosses_rim`, `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:193`).
- The new test is non-vacuous. I checked this three ways. The change lives only in the no-model branch, so the pin fails on main's law. The pin asserts the exact move index (42) and the row line (y 60). The author's M1 mutation (no vertex crossing) fails the pin, as the table in the body says.
- The guard keeps the gouge side. A vertex touch with both neighbours on one side is not a crossing. The sim pin proves it, and the #43 corner pin still holds.
- The code fails closed. `Trace::Unread` never reads as a crossing. A NaN radius or a NaN vertex never passes the band or the sign tests. Degenerate traces (`len2` at or below the touch band, loops with fewer than three points) read as no crossing, so the move answers to the walls.
- Law checks pass. Touched files stay under 400 lines. The new app test sits in the lowest crate that defines what it drives, and its Gate map names that crate. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` on any user path. The decision file is present. Provenance lines are intact. The body is complete (`Changelog:`, `Fixes #1659`). No process files changed.

## Results

Ran on the self-hosted pr-test runner (macOS, `m3`): https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43609155751

- Head confirmed: the run refused any other head. Trial merge with main `2b6e03f20`: clean.
- Quick gate: sim suites green (5 binaries, 174 tests). App suites green (6 binaries, 34 tests). All five new pins passed on the merged tree.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No per-OS `cfg` lines in the diff, so no local re-run was owed. The ui suites are not in the quick plan (no UI change).

## Issue #1669

This PR does not resolve #1669. It leaves it open. The vertex test uses the exact sign `su * sw < 0.0` (`crates/sim/src/verify/arc_wall.rs:139`). The arc test uses the same rule on the radius (`crates/sim/src/verify/arc_wall.rs:215`). So a wall that runs along the trace, with a wobble of any non-zero size, can read as a crossing if one of its vertices stands on the line. #1669 asks for a distance band here. This head adds none. Note two facts for triage. The same exact sign is already the law in `proper_cross` (`crates/sim/src/verify/laws.rs:47`), so this PR does not widen the exposure. But a false excuse can pass a gouge, which is the worst class in the Prime Directive. The maintainer may want to weigh #1669's rating. #1669 does not block this PR: the repro case needs a collinear wobble, and no known geometry produces one today.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The arc branch of `Trace::through` has no direct pin. A Face row is a straight move, so the gap is narrow. It is also named in #1669.
- `Trace::Poly` reads the vertex pass against the footprint pieces, without the pad. That direction is conservative: it excuses fewer moves.
- I could not find why the stock outline carries side vertices, as the body says. The fix reads them correctly either way. That question fits #1669 or a small follow-up.

## What was not exercised

- The batch and release tiers.
- The GUI and the pixel snapshots.
- The arc branch of `Trace::through` (no pin).
- A wobble wall along the trace (the #1669 case) — not tested here, and not excused by this PR.
- A Windows local build. The runner gate was macOS; the diff holds no OS-specific readings.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
